name: Green River
label: Sub Pop
lede: Three years, two EPs and one album, and when they split on Halloween 1987 the pieces became Mudhoney, Mother Love Bone and eventually Pearl Jam.

eras.title: The worst band in town, and a darker name
eras.text: Mark Arm and Steve Turner came up in Mr. Epp and the Calculations, a Bellevue punk band Arm has said enjoyed being called the worst in Seattle. In 1984 they pulled in Jeff Ament, Alex Vincent and Stone Gossard and named the new band after something much grimmer.

years.h: Mark Arm uses the word grunge to insult his own band
years.p: Writing to the Seattle fanzine Desperate Times under his real name, Mark McLaughlin, Arm describes Mr. Epp as pure grunge. It's often cited as the word's first Seattle use.

years.h: Green River forms: Arm, Turner, Ament, Vincent, then Gossard
years.p: Mark Arm and Steve Turner recruit bassist Jeff Ament from Deranged Diction and drummer Alex Vincent. Stone Gossard, a high school friend of Turner and Vincent, joins after the first rehearsal at Turner's Mercer Island home.
years.xp: Ament met Arm and Turner through a Seattle coffee shop job; he didn't think much of Mr. Epp but was fed up with Deranged Diction. The name Green River came to Arm and Turner separately. Arm has pointed to Green River College and the Creedence song, but the name also nodded to the Green River Killer, then all over the Washington news. Turner later called it a dumb joke.

years.h: Green River's first demos at Reciprocal Recording
years.p: The band cuts its first demos at Seattle's Reciprocal Recording. They stay in the vault until a 2016 vinyl release.

years.cap: Green River at Sub Pop 20, 2008 · Wikimedia
years.h: Green River's first Seattle gig
years.p: Green River play their first show in Seattle in July 1984, a mix of [[The Stooges|794c6bf2-3241-416f-9b8f-24e2d84a1c4b]] punk and '70s hard rock that no one yet had a word for.

eras.title: Turner walks, the tour flops
eras.text: The band's first record took so long that its guitarist quit before it came out. Steve Turner wanted garage rock; the others wanted Aerosmith. Bruce Fairweather came in, a national tour went badly, and the band still made friends like Sonic Youth along the way.

q: I should not be in this band. I'm fighting them so hard.
years.h: Steve Turner quits Green River, Bruce Fairweather replaces him
years.p: Steve Turner, into 1960s garage rock, [[Billy Childish|23ef9155-df05-4e3a-8109-acb603f3146d]] and [[The Replacements|dc0d05ce-2f47-4962-b4fa-8631a0a51987]], leaves as Green River get heavier. Fairweather, Ament's old Deranged Diction bandmate, takes his place.
years.xp: Alex Vincent said the music got a little more rock once Turner left. Turner went back to school and, in 1988, into [[Mudhoney|e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc]].

years.h: Come on Down on Homestead: often called the first grunge record
years.p: Green River's debut EP comes out on New York's Homestead Records. It sells poorly, but it's often called the first record by a grunge band.
years.xp: [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] later nodded to the title track in their song Nevermind (What Was It Anyway).

years.h: Green River's first U.S. tour: dead crowds and a broken mic
years.p: Touring behind Come on Down, Green River open for [[Dead Kennedys|37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e]] in San Francisco to an indifferent crowd. At a show with [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]] the PA fails and Mark Arm throws the microphones into the audience.
years.xp: Big Black withheld Green River's pay to cover a lost expensive microphone. [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] told Rolling Stone that everybody acts like an asshole when he's a kid. A planned tour with the U.K. Subs fell apart over visas, so Green River played CBGB's and Hoboken with The U-Men instead.

years.h: Deep Six: Green River on the first grunge compilation
years.p: C/Z Records' Deep Six puts Green River's 10,000 Things and Your Own Best Friend next to [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]], [[Soundgarden|153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4]], [[Skin Yard|0119843b-4d56-47b6-ac0d-11528259bf0a]], [[Malfunkshun|71f4a8ff-97ba-47c6-a729-7f87de77c796]] and The U-Men.

years.h: Together We'll Never, recorded onto Betamax tapes
years.p: Stuck waiting for money to finish a Sub Pop EP, Green River release a 7-inch on Tasque Force, cut by engineer Gordon Raphael on an Akai deck that recorded to Betamax cassettes.

eras.title: Ultra-loose, then over
eras.text: Green River gave Bruce Pavitt's Sub Pop its first real record, and Sub Pop gave the scene its word. By the end of the year the band had split down the middle: punk on one side, arena rock on the other.

q: Ultra-loose GRUNGE that destroyed the morals of a generation.
years.h: Dry as a Bone: Sub Pop's first non-compilation release
years.p: Recorded in summer 1986 with [[Jack Endino|d06cca33-9167-4049-b5ce-6a6aeff60a8d]] and held up for lack of money, the EP comes out as Sub Pop SP-11. Pavitt's catalog pitches it as grunge that destroyed a generation's morals.
years.xp:
Endino remembered the band as serious and meticulous in the studio. At the release show there was a green cake, and by the end of the night, Endino said, green frosting was on everything.

Pavitt later admitted the catalog line was complete hyperbole. It stuck anyway.

years.h: Jeff Ament packs a Los Angeles guest list with label people
years.p: Opening for [[Jane's Addiction|e3434cc7-d348-491a-9dc8-325af3d9086d]] at the Scream in Los Angeles, Green River find Jeff Ament has filled the guest list with major-label reps instead of friends. Only two show up.
years.xp: Arm, blowing out his voice after a San Francisco show, thought the set was terrible. Ament loved Jane's Addiction and came home wanting more of that kind of career. Arm thought Ament and Gossard had turned careerist.

years.h: Green River break up at Halloween rehearsal
years.p: At rehearsal on October 31, Jeff Ament, Stone Gossard and Bruce Fairweather tell Mark Arm and Alex Vincent they're leaving. The band agrees to finish Rehab Doll first.
years.xp: Arm wanted to go further into Australian punk like [[Feedtime|4775deb5-f3c3-45e2-b6c3-b66678aae511]] and [[The Scientists|b2cd8f3d-7049-4ebf-a5d6-52c08f6a59c0]]; Ament and Gossard wanted big Aerosmith-style rock. Arm told Rolling Stone it felt like a weight off his shoulders. Vincent called it a terrible Halloween and said he was devastated.

eras.title: One band becomes three
eras.text: Green River's pieces scattered fast. Arm and Turner made Mudhoney; Ament, Gossard and Fairweather found singer Andrew Wood and formed Mother Love Bone, and Wood's death sent Ament and Gossard toward Pearl Jam.

years.h: Mark Arm and Steve Turner start [[Mudhoney|e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc]]
years.p: Two months after the split, Arm and Turner hold their first Mudhoney practice with [[Matt Lukin|299e8c0a-63ad-4d49-b492-d3740364da84]] and [[Dan Peters|3402566b-20dc-47f1-973b-2af1dedae702]].

years.cap: Mark Arm at the Green River reunion, 2008 · Wikimedia
years.h: Ament, Gossard and Fairweather form [[Mother Love Bone|a5585acd-9b65-49a7-a63b-3cc4ee18846e]] with Andrew Wood
years.p: The three ex-Green River players team up with [[Malfunkshun|71f4a8ff-97ba-47c6-a729-7f87de77c796]] singer Andrew Wood in Mother Love Bone, the glam-leaning band Ament and Gossard had wanted all along.

years.h: Rehab Doll: Green River's only album, out after the split
years.p: Finished after the breakup, Rehab Doll comes out on Sub Pop. Arm sings One More Stitch lying under a grand piano and Fairweather plays sitar.
years.xp: [[Kim Gordon|19301485-ac9c-4dad-885b-cd8e8c8b4184]] of [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] sang on the record, but most of her vocals were mixed out; Endino restored them on the later deluxe edition. Vincent called the big, triggered drum sound grunge meets Poison.

years.h: Mother Love Bone singer Andrew Wood dies of a heroin overdose
years.p: Andrew Wood dies of a heroin overdose days before Mother Love Bone's debut album is due. Ament and Gossard go on to [[Temple of the Dog|e9571c17-817f-4d34-ae3f-0c7a96f822c1]] with [[Chris Cornell|cbf9738d-8f81-4a92-bc64-ede09341652d]], then Pearl Jam.

years.h: Dry as a Bone/Rehab Doll on one CD
years.p: Sub Pop combines Green River's EP and album on a single CD as the Seattle sound starts to sell.

eras.title: Three guitars, one more time
eras.text: Green River came back only for the occasional party. By the time they did, two of them were in Pearl Jam, two were in Mudhoney, and the old argument about punk versus rock didn't matter much.

years.h: Green River reunite for two songs at a Pearl Jam show
years.p: During a Pearl Jam concert in Las Vegas, Arm, Turner, Ament and Gossard play Swallow My Pride and Ain't Nothing to Do, with [[Chuck Treece|ef661f53-d4b4-4903-811c-f3dcb1b970f3]] drumming for Alex Vincent, who was living in Japan.

years.h: A 1987 demo of Swallow My Pride lands on the Hype! soundtrack
years.p: Doug Pray's grunge documentary Hype! puts Green River's 1987 demo on its Sub Pop soundtrack.

years.h: All six Green River members warm up at the Sunset Tavern
years.p: For the first time since the '80s, all six members play together, at Seattle's Sunset Tavern in Ballard.

years.h: Green River play Sub Pop's 20th anniversary at Marymoor Park
years.p: Green River reunite with a three-guitar lineup for Sub Pop's birthday. Turner called it a three-guitar army and said it was really fun.

years.h: Green River join dates on the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]]' 25th anniversary tour
years.p: The reunited band plays a few more shows on the Melvins' anniversary run, then stops again.

years.h: Green River's 1984 demos come out on vinyl
years.p: The June 1984 Reciprocal Recording demos, made before Stone Gossard joined, finally get a release.

years.h: Live at the Tropicana on Jackpot Records
years.p: An archival live LP of Green River comes out on Portland's Jackpot Records.

sources.title: Rolling Stone: Green River and Seattle's First 'Grunge' Album: The Oral History
